text_blocks.snippet: Bacterial vaginosis (BV) is not typically considered a sexually transmitted disease (STD). However, it is thought to be associated with sexual activity and may be transmitted through contact with an infected partner.
snippet_highlighted_words: not typically considered a sexually transmitted disease (STD)

text_blocks.snippet: Studies have shown that BV is more common in sexually active women and that the risk of developing BV increases with the number of sexual partners. Additionally, BV is more likely to occur in women who have other STDs.

While BV is not an STD, it is important to be aware of the potential for sexual transmission and to take precautions to prevent it. If you or your partner have BV, it is recommended to seek medical treatment to prevent complications and reduce the risk of transmitting it to others.
